cards.title: New parchi? Ask before you leave
cards.body: Questions about a new prescription usually show up three days later. Ask them at the clinic or the chemist counter instead.

cards.title: What is this for?
cards.body: Knowing the reason helps your parent take it seriously, and helps you notice if two medicines seem to overlap.

cards.title: When and how to take it
cards.body: Morning or night, before or after food, with water or milk. Get it written down in plain words.

cards.title: For how long?
cards.body: A few days, until the strip finishes, or ongoing? Don't assume. Ask clearly.

cards.title: Which side effects to watch for
cards.body: Ask what's common, what's worth a call, and what needs urgent attention.

cards.title: Does it clash with current medicines?
cards.body: Show the doctor and chemist everything your parent already takes, including from other doctors. Mix-ups hide here.

cards.title: What if a dose is missed?
cards.body: Ask now so nobody guesses later. The answer can be different for different medicines.

cards.title: Six questions, one less worry
cards.body: Write the answers on the prescription or save a note on your phone. Future you will be grateful.

takeaway: For every new prescription, ask what it's for, how and how long to take it, side effects, clashes and missed doses.
share: Screenshot this before the next clinic visit.
